newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-NZ Barbarians "best team in the world".
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-NZ Barbarians "best team in the world".

text.p: LONDON, Nov 28 - England rugby captain Phil de Glanville, continuing his side's down-beat build-up to Saturday's international, has lavished praise on the New Zealand Barbarians, NZPA reports.

Sean Fitzpatrick's tourists may be well short of a full All Black test side, but that didn't prevent de Glanville, who led England out for the first time last Saturday, describing them as "the best team in the world".
At least seven first choice All Blacks -- nearly half a team -- are missing from the Barbarians side.
Commenting on the possible absence of Jonah Lomu because of a groin infection, de Glanville said: "If Lomu cannot play, his replacement will be Glen Osborne, who is a fantastic footballer.
"We are coming up against the best team in the world. Any nation that goes to South Africa and wins a series has to be thoroughly respected. And we have to have a realistic approach.
"We are not playing mind games. We are going out there to learn.
"We have a young side and we are trying to develop our game against the highest quality rugby players that are now around."

De Glanville added that, like New Zealand a few years ago, England were in a rebuilding situation and, also like New Zealand, they should be prepared to lose the occasional game to develop their style.
"We are still in the same early-doors situation that the All Blacks faced a couple of years ago. We are young. We want to develop onwards and upwards," de Glanville added.
De Glanville conceded that sometimes European teams were in awe of the southern hemisphere big three.
"The north has gone on bended knee to Australia, New Zealand and South Africa, but we do have the capacity to beat them in one-off games," he said.
